teaching: Names can be given, but not permanent labels: Pluto, a country's borders and a hundred-dollar bill change with the names we keep in mind, while the thing itself stays as it is (Tao Te Ching, Chapter 1, Thomas Cleary translation).
youtube_title: Names Can Be Given, but Not Permanent Labels

word_overrides.why: the user asked to start at 'the country of Mexico'; 'you know' before it is cut
medium.en 'Okay.' after 'label.' is room tone (the clip ends at 2281.0)
large-v3 hears 'so, so individually'; the first 'so' (2125.9-2126.14) is before the cut, the second starts at 2126.56 on the envelope
large-v3 and small.en hear 'the name' twice (medium.en 'a name'); 'You' starts at 2207.06 on the envelope; medium.en's 'Thank you.' after 'right?' is room tone
medium.en mishears this line ('I hope that's'); large-v3 (narrow pass) hears 'But no matter what the name is, the reality is still there.' The 1.1 s pause inside 'no ... matter' is trimmed

phrases: It's no longer | named a planet.
It has nothing | to do with *Pluto.
We can give names | and *labels to things,
The country of *Mexico | used to include
and go all the way | up to *Wyoming.
in that western part | of the United States?
In order for a | hundred dollar bill
that it's a | hundred dollar bill.
If all of us | were to *stop thinking
that it was a | hundred dollar bill,
You can have a *reality | without having the name,
But no matter | what the *name is,

image.note: photograph of the Moon (Copernicus crater), a world whose name is ours: 'Names can be given, but not permanent labels' (on the join, after Pluto)
Bierstadt's Yosemite valley: 'the country of Mexico used to include California…' (on the join)
Bierstadt's western mountain under storm clouds: 'what changed in that western part…? Nothing changed but the label' (on the join)
Swedish copper plate money, 1731: money is a thing 'we sustain… with our intention and our thoughts'
Hokusai's Red Fuji: 'no matter what the name is, the reality is still there' (on the join; under the end-card dissolve)
